newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Issue news hits Savings Bank on Estonian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Issue news hits Savings Bank on Estonian bourse.

text.p: Savings Bank fell on Monday after it said it would issue shares below market levels but later recovered during lively trade on the Estonian bourse.
Overall volume on the main list was 8.9 million kroons and the Tallinn stock exchange index fell 0.63 percent to 96.77.
Free market trade came to 1.9 million kroons and the list was joined by a new company, the Rakvere meat processing plant.

Savings Bank turned over 1.3 million kroons of stock and fell after it announced it would issue shares at 33.50 kroons. It hit a low of 33.75 kroons but climbed back to close at 34.85 kroons, versus a 36.55 kroons close on Friday.
"After the announcement, the Savings Bank shares fell but then investors found that the stock was cheap and they bought it again," said Toomas Tsopp, a trader at Tallinnapank.
Savings Bank is to issue 3.2 million of the new shares.
Shares in Tallinnapank were the most traded on the main list, registering business of 4.9 million kroons and ending slightly higher at 38.89 kroons.

Rakvere traded 270,000 kroons of stock during its first day on the free market and it closed at 3.35 kroons. Tallinn Pharmaceutical factory was the most traded at almost one million kroons and it closed half a kroon down at 46.50 kroons.
